À Malte, le référendum maltais sur l'adhésion à l'Union européenne recueille 53,5 % de oui.
Jean-Paul II, dans son exhortation apostolique Ecclesia in Europa, lance un cri d'alarme contre l'abandon de la culture chrétienne en Europe.
L'ouragan Charley tue 27 personnes en Floride, 4 à Cuba et 1 en Jamaïque.
Lancement du célèbre réseau social, Facebook.
Le président des États-Unis George W. Bush est réélu pour un second mandat de 4 ans.
L'ouragan Ivan provoque 37 morts à Grenade, 5 au Venezuela et 4 en République dominicaine.
L'ouragan Frances fait 10 morts en Floride.
Entrée en vigueur de la suspension de l'enrichissement d'uranium par l'Iran, conformément à l'accord de Paris.
Incendie dans un supermarché d'Asuncion au Paraguay avec un lourd bilan : 399 morts, 144 disparus.
Anniversaire de l'arrivée des Français en Amérique du Nord (1604).
Menacés par les débordements d'une manifestation dirigée contre eux à Abidjan, des militaires français tirent provoquant sept à soixante morts selon les sources.
Ouverture du salon de l'E3 qui se déroule du 15 au 18 mai.
8 concerts géants Live 8 pour l'annulation de la dette des pays d'Afrique à Paris, Londres, Berlin, Philadelphie, Moscou, Johannesburg, Tokyo et Rome.
Kirghizistan : renversement du gouvernement par la Révolution des Tulipes.
Mahmoud Abbas remporte l'élection présidentielle.
L'Iran prévient que sa décision de reprendre la conversion d'uranium, préalable à l'enrichissement, est « irréversible ».
Trois attentats au sein de la capitale Amman provoquent plus de 60 morts et 300 blessés.
Élection de Ma Ying-jeou, maire de la capitale de Taïwan, Taipei, comme président du Kuomintang (KMT), devenant le principal dirigeant de la première force de l'opposition.
Le cardinal Joseph Ratzinger est élu pape sous le nom de Benoît XVI.
Par son arrêt Roper vs. Simmons, acquis par cinq voix contre quatre, la Cour suprême des États-Unis interdit la peine de mort pour les criminels mineurs au moment des faits.
La Corée du Nord déclare posséder l'arme nucléaire, deux ans après s'être retirée du Traité de non-prolifération nucléaire.
Arrestation d'Abou Faraj al-Libbi, officier d'Al-Qaïda, au Pakistan.
Après une odyssée de sept ans et de près de cinq milliards de kilomètres dans l'espace, la sonde spatiale américaine Stardust retourne sur Terre avec sa précieuse cargaison de poussières cométaires.

Au Québec, entrée en vigueur d'une loi anti-tabac stricte, identique à celle déjà adoptée à plusieurs endroits en Amérique du Nord, interdisant formellement l'usage du tabac dans tous les bars et restaurants de la province.
Admission du Monténégro à l'ONU en tant que État membre.

Cap-Vert : le Parti africain pour l'indépendance du Cap-Vert (PAICV, socialiste) obtient 52,3 % des voix et 41 sièges sur 72 à l’Assemblée nationale, se maintenant ainsi au pouvoir auquel il avait accédé il y a 5 ans.
Quatre condamnés à mort japonais ont été exécutés par pendaison, levant ainsi un moratoire de facto sur la peine capitale qui était en vigueur depuis 15 mois au Japon.
Fête chrétienne de Noël dans le calendrier de l'Église russe orthodoxe.
Élections présidentielle et législatives.
Lancement réussi de New Horizons, la première sonde spatiale à destination de la planète Pluton.
Le Premier ministre éthiopien Meles Zenawi a annoncé que son pays était en guerre contre les islamistes somaliens officialisant l'intervention déjà en cours depuis plusieurs semaines.
Arrestation de 18 suspects dans le démantèlement d'une cellule terroriste dans la région de Toronto, au Canada.
Littérature : Sortie de la version anglaise de Harry Potter et les Reliques de la Mort, dernier tome de la série Harry Potter.

Espace : annonce, par l'équipe de Stéphane Udry, de l'Observatoire de Genève, de la découverte de 'Gliese 581 c', première exoplanète située dans la zone habitable de son étoile, Gliese 581, à 20,5 années-lumière du Soleil.
Canada : Tous les jeux vidéo vendus au Québec doivent être 'obligatoirement' traduits en français.
Amérique du Nord : Les Ducks d'Anaheim remportent la Coupe Stanley.
Espace : L’Agence spatiale européenne (ESA) annonce que la sonde spatiale Rosetta est arrivé à proximité de Mars.

Proche-Orient : début de la visite officielle, jusqu’au 13 février, du président russe Vladimir Poutine, en Arabie saoudite — à laquelle il propose une coopération dans le domaine nucléaire —, au Qatar et en Jordanie.
États-Unis : Barack Obama, 45 ans, sénateur démocrate de l'Illinois, annonce sa candidature à la présidence des États-Unis devant le capitole de Springfield, capitale de l'Illinois.
Science : Annonce de la découverte du transfert électrique sans fil.
Le Président du Venezuela, Hugo Chávez effectue en parallèle, une tournée de visites officielles anti-Bush, en Argentine, au Nicaragua, en Haïti et à la Jamaïque.
États-Unis : le FBI annonce avoir découvert un groupe suspecté de préparer un attentat contre les réserves de carburant de l'aéroport John F. Kennedy de New York.
Tchéquie : un pont s'est effondré sur la trajectoire d'un train, entrainant quatre morts et une quarantaine de blessés dans la collision.
Islande : la Banque centrale islandaise renonce à maintenir un taux de change fixe entre la couronne et l'euro pour tenter d’enrayer la dévaluation de sa monnaie.
Abkhazie : à la suite de l'indépendance du Kosovo, la Russie lève désormais toutes ses restrictions commerciales à l'encontre de la région pro-russes et sécessionniste de la Géorgie.

Kosovo : L'Estonie, l'Italie, le Danemark et le Luxembourg reconnaissent officiellement le nouvel État indépendant ce qui monte à 16 le nombre d'Etats indépendants à établir des liens diplomatiques avec le Kosovo.
Malte (lire maltaise) et Chypre (livre chypriote) sont les 14e et 15e États de l'Union à adopter l'euro.
Kosovo : Le Liechtenstein reconnaît officiellement l'indépendance du nouvel État.
Kosovo : La Bulgarie, la Croatie, la Hongrie et Monaco reconnaissent officiellement l'indépendance du nouvel État.
Afrique : Le Président George W. Bush entame une série de visites officielles de six jours qui l'amèneront, au Bénin, au Liberia, en Tanzanie, au Rwanda, au Ghana et au Libéria.
Proche-Orient - Iran : le Président Nicolas Sarkozy entame une tournée de visites, jusqu'au 15 janvier, en Arabie saoudite, au Qatar et aux Émirats arabes unis.
Atterrissage sur Mars de la sonde spatiale Phoenix.
La NASA provoque deux crashs sur la Lune, dont celui de la sonde LCROSS, pour savoir s'il y a de l'eau sur le satellite.
Mort de l'artiste Michael Jackson ; mort de l'actrice Farrah Fawcett ; mort de l'artiste Sky Saxon ; mort de la sportive Zinaida Stahurskaia.
Pour le anniversaire de la Révolution de Velours (Slovaquie).
Pour l'année européenne de la créativité et de l'innovation (Saint-Marin).
Barack Obama obtient le prix Nobel de la paix.
En représailles à la mort dans un attentat la veille du chef d'état-major de l'armée Batista Tagme Na Waie, le président João Bernardo Vieira est assassiné par des militaires.
Comores : le Vol 626 Yemenia au départ de l'aéroport de Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle s'abîme en mer au large du pays avec 142 passagers et 11 membres d'équipage.
Ouverture à Istanbul du 5e Forum mondial de l'eau.
Le skieur français Jean-Baptiste Grange met un terme à sa saison à la suite d'une blessure aux ligaments croisés du genou contractée lors de la descente de Beaver Creek.

Décollage de la navette spatiale Américaine Atlantis depuis Cap Kennedy en Floride, sous le nom de mission STS-125. Il s'agit de la cinquième et dernière mission d'entretien du télescope spatial Hubble.
Fermeture de tous les aéroports du nord de l'Europe à la suite de l'éruption de l'Eyjafjöll, en Islande.
Éclipse totale de Soleil visible depuis l'Amérique du Sud.
Au Kirghizistan, à la suite de l'emprisonnement de membres de l'opposition, une révolte populaire a lieu dans les rues de Bichkek.
Chili : un séisme d'une magnitude de 8,8 sur l'échelle de Richter frappe durement le pays.
Inscription du Repas gastronomique des Français au patrimoine de l'Unesco.
Inauguration du gratte-ciel Burj Khalifa, qui établit un nouveau record de hauteur.
La sonde spatiale européenne Rosetta survole l'astéroïde (21) Lutèce.
Un séisme d'une magnitude de 7,7 accompagné d'un tsunami et l'éruption volcanique du volcan Merapi touchent l'Indonésie.
États-Unis : Apple annonce sa tablette numérique nommée iPad, qui est un mélange entre le Macintosh et l'iPhone.
Une tentative de coup d'État en Équateur est réprimée par le gouvernement de Rafael Correa.
Réunion du Forum pour le futur à Doha (Qatar).
Arrivée de la sonde MESSENGER en orbite autour de Mercure.
Proclamation de l'indépendance du Soudan du Sud.
83e cérémonie des Oscars au Kodak Theater à Los Angeles.
Super Bowl XLV, finale annuelle de la National Football League de football américain, à Arlington, Texas.
Le Portrait de Paul Éluard de Salvador Dalí est vendu aux enchères par Sotheby's à Londres pour 15,8 millions d'euros, record pour une œuvre du peintre espagnol.
Tallinn, capitale de l’Estonie, et Turku, ville finlandaise, désignées Capitales européennes de la culture.
WrestleMania XXVII, événement annuel de catch, au Georgia Dome d'Atlanta, Géorgie, États-Unis.
Aux États-Unis, à Pittsburgh dans l'État de Pennsylvanie, édition de la Classique hivernale de la Ligue nationale de hockey.
Année internationale de la chimie par l’Assemblée générale des Nations unies, initiative qui souligne le anniversaire du prix Nobel de chimie accordé à Marie Curie.
Éclipse solaire annulaire, parcours : Pacifique, Asie, Amérique du Nord.
Éclipse solaire totale, parcours : Australie, Nouvelle-Zélande, Amérique du Sud et océan Pacifique.
Arrivée du robot Curiosity sur Mars (Mars Science Laboratory).
Vladimir Poutine prend ses fonctions de président de la fédération russe.
Gangnam Style de Psy atteint le milliard de vues sur YouTube.
14 octobre (Autriche et Nouveau-Mexique) : Felix Baumgartner fait un saut record : celui du saut le plus haut (38969,4 m).
(France) : second tour de l'élection présidentielle française : François Hollande (Parti socialiste) est élu Président de la République Française avec trois points d’avance sur Nicolas Sarkozy.
L'Ouragan Sandy, parti de la mer des Caraïbes, atteint la côte est des États-Unis.
La capitalisation boursière d'Apple dépasse celle du géant de l'informatique Microsoft avec 622 milliards de dollars.
Année Rousseau à l'occasion du tricentenaire de sa naissance.
Lancement de la sonde Chang'e 3 en direction de la Lune.
Le président américain, Barack Obama, se rend en visite officielle de trois jours en Israël et en Palestine.
Inauguration à Istanbul, en Turquie, du Marmaray, ligne ferroviaire avec tunnel passant sous le Bosphore.
Un incendie de forêt au Colorado provoque la mort de deux personnes.
Lors d'un discours à l'Université Nazarbaïev à Astana au Kazakhstan, le président Xi Jinping annonce officiellement le projet de Nouvelle route de la soie.
L'Argentin Jorge Mario Bergoglio est élu pape et prend le nom de François.
Au Vatican, à la suite de la renonciation du pontificat de Benoît XVI, début du conclave pour désigner le 266e pape.
Un accident de car en soirée sur un viaduc de l'autoroute A16 Naples-Bari (Italie) fait près de 40 victimes, dont de nombreux enfants.
Xi Jinping est élu président de la république populaire de Chine par l'Assemblée nationale populaire.
En Centrafrique, le chef d'État François Bozizé fuit les rebelles et Michel Djotodia se proclame président.
Andreï Kobiakov est nommé Premier ministre de Biélorussie.
En Ukraine, le Parlement vote la libération de l’opposante Ioulia Tymochenko, la destitution du président et la tenue d’une nouvelle élection présidentielle.
Élections législatives aux Fidji, remportées par le parti Fidji d'abord du Premier ministre.
La Lettonie adopte l'euro à la place du lats et devient le membre de la zone euro.
Année internationale de la cristallographie et Année internationale de l'agriculture familiale par l’Assemblée générale des Nations unies.
Sommet d'Ottawa entre le Canada et l'Union européenne - Annonce de l'Accord économique et commercial global (AECG) ou (CETA) acronyme en anglais.
Référendum d'autodétermination en Crimée.
Incendie de la Maison des syndicats d'Odessa (Ukraine).
Élection présidentielle en Turquie, Recep Tayyip Erdoğan est élu au premier tour.
Le prix Nobel de la paix est attribué à l'adolescente pakistanaise Malala Yousafzai et à l'Indien Kailash Satyarthi pour leur combat contre l'exploitation des enfants.
Dans la série télévisée Fringe, les Observateurs, des êtres humains venus de l'an 2609, voyagent vers le passé et envahissent la Terre.
Serge Venturini reçoit le prix international Grégoire de Narek à Erevan en Arménie.
Championnats du monde d'athlétisme à Pékin au Stade national.
Éclipse solaire partielle visible dans le sud de l'Afrique et dans l'Antarctique.
Élection présidentielle en Ouzbékistan, Islom Karimov est réélu.
Le Championnat du monde de handball masculin se déroule au Qatar.
Lancement de TurkmenAlem52E/MonacoSAT, premier satellite artificiel du Turkménistan.
La Côte d'Ivoire remporte la Coupe d'Afrique des nations de football en Guinée équatoriale.
Assassinat à Moscou de Boris Nemtsov, opposant de Vladimir Poutine.
57e cérémonie des Grammy Awards à Los Angeles (États-Unis).

textEn: A farmers' revolt begins in the Midwestern United States.
Hergé's Tintin in America (Tintin en Amérique) concludes serial publication and is issued in book format (in black and white) in Belgium.
Beginning of the Chaco War between Paraguay and Bolivia because of delimitation problems and others.
German art dealer Otto Wacker is sentenced to 19 months in prison for selling fraudulent paintings he attributed to Vincent van Gogh.
Sakuradamon Incident: Korean nationalist Lee Bong-chang fails in his effort to assassinate Emperor Hirohito of Japan.
Mahatma Gandhi begins a hunger strike in Poona prison, India.
Massive riots between Hindus and Muslims in Bombay leave thousands dead and injured.
Hattie W. Caraway of Arkansas becomes the first woman to be elected to the United States Senate, succeeding her late husband, Thaddeus Caraway, in a special election,.
British geneticist J. B. S. Haldane publishes The Causes of Evolution, unifying the findings of Mendelian genetics with those of evolutionary science.
Haile Selassie announces an anti-slavery law in Abyssinia.
Chaco War: Paraguay formally declares war on Bolivia.

Scientist Albert Einstein arrives from Europe in the United States, where he settles permanently as a refugee from Nazi Germany and takes up a position at the Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton, New Jersey.
The first flight over Mount Everest is made by the British Houston-Mount Everest Flight Expedition, led by the Marquis of Clydesdale, and funded by Lucy, Lady Houston.
Gandhi is sentenced to prison in India.
The International Court of Justice in The Hague decides that Greenland belongs to Denmark, and condemns Norwegian landings on eastern Greenland.
American airship Akron crashes off the coast of New Jersey, killing 73 of its 76 crewmen.
Loggers cause a forest fire in the Coast Range of Oregon, later known as the first forest fire of the Tillamook Burn.
The detection by Karl Jansky of radio waves from the center of the Milky Way Galaxy is reported in The New York Times.
The first rugby union test match is played between the Wallabies of Australia and the Springboks of South Africa, at Newlands in Cape Town.
Turkey concludes a treaty with the creditors of the former Ottoman Empire to schedule the payments in Paris (Turkey succeeds in clearing all the debt in less than twenty years).
The Yomiuri Giants, a successful professional baseball club in Japan, is founded in Tokyo.
Abidjan becomes the capital of the French colony of Ivory Coast.
A typhoon in Osaka and Kyoto, Japan, kills 1,660, injures 5,400, and destroys the rice harvest.
Winter – Tadj ol-Molouk, Empress consort of Iran, and her daughters appear publicly in Tehran without a veil, leading to its abolition in the country.
Donald Duck makes his film debut in Walt Disney's Silly Symphony cartoon The Wise Little Hen.
November 5 – The MacRobertson Air Race is flown from RAF Mildenhall in England to Melbourne, Australia, to celebrate the centenary of the state of Victoria.
The Muroto typhoon in Honshū, Japan kills 3,036 people, and destroys the temple, schools, and other buildings in Osaka.
King Alexander of Yugoslavia is assassinated, while French foreign minister Louis Barthou is accidentally killed by the French police, during the king's state visit in Marseille.
Adolf Hitler and Benito Mussolini meet for the first time, at the Venice Biennale.
November 3 – Charles Kingsford Smith makes the first eastward crossing of the Pacific Ocean, from his native Brisbane, Australia, to San Francisco, in the Lockheed Altair Lady Southern Cross.
Sun Myung Moon, a teenage Presbyterian convert in Korea under Japanese rule, claims to have a revelation from Jesus, telling him to complete his mission from almost 2,000 years ago.
The Chaco War between Paraguay and Bolivia ends.

Dust Bowl: "Black Sunday", the great dust storm in the United States hits eastern New Mexico and Colorado, and western Oklahoma the hardest (it will be made famous by Woody Guthrie, in his "dust bowl ballads").
The first canned beer is sold in Richmond, Virginia, United States, by Gottfried Krueger Brewing Company.
In China, Mao Zedong issues the Wayaobu Manifesto, On Tactics Against Japanese Imperialism, calling for a National United Front against the Japanese invasion.
Hanshin Tigers, a well known professional baseball club of Japan, is founded in Osaka.
Italian premier Benito Mussolini and French Foreign Minister Pierre Laval conclude an agreement, in which each power agrees not to oppose the other's colonial claims.
James J. Braddock defeats Max Baer at Madison Square Garden Bowl, to win the heavyweight boxing championship of the world.
Ten people, including musician Carlos Gardel, are killed in a collision between two Ford Trimotor airplanes at Olaya Herrera Airport in Medellín, Colombia.
Robert Watson-Watt first demonstrates the use of radar to detect aircraft, at Daventry in the UK.
Speaking in Rome, Benito Mussolini announces the foundation of the empire, as Italian East Africa is formed from the Italian territories of Eritrea, Ethiopia and Italian Somaliland.
March of the Iron Will: Italian forces occupy Addis Ababa unopposed.
May 28 - Alan Turing submits "On Computable Numbers", proving the undecidability of the Halting problem and the decision problem for logic.
The Canadian Broadcasting Corporation (CBC) begins radio in Canada.
Radium E (bismuth-210) becomes the first radioactive element to be made synthetically.
The last known thylacine ("Tasmanian tiger")dies in Hobart Zoo in Tasmania.
Focke-Wulf Fw 61, the first fully controllable helicopter, makes its maiden flight.
Xi'an Incident: Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek of the Republic of China is kidnapped by Marshal Zhang Xueliang.
In response to a polio outbreak, Chicago Public Schools launches a distance education program which constitutes the first large-scale use of radio broadcasts to facilitate distance education.
In violation of the Treaty of Versailles and Locarno Treaties, Nazi Germany reoccupies the Rhineland.
July – The Dáil Éireann debates and passes the new draft Constitution of Ireland, which is then submitted for public approval by plebiscite.

Yekatit 12: During a public ceremony at the Viceregal Palace (the former Imperial residence) in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, two Eritrean nationalists attempt to kill viceroy Rodolfo Graziani with a number of grenades.
Abraham Lincoln's head is dedicated at Mount Rushmore.
Walt Disney's Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs, the world's first feature-length cel animated film, premieres at the Carthay Circle Theatre in Los Angeles.
George Allen & Unwin, Ltd. of London publishes the first edition of J. R. R. Tolkien's The Hobbit.
The Geibeltbad Pirna water sports facility is opened in Dresden, Germany.
At the age of 70, conductor Arturo Toscanini conducts the NBC Symphony Orchestra on radio for the first time, beginning his successful 17-year tenure with that orchestra.
Ernest Hemingway's novel To Have and Have Not is first published, in the United States.
The first total solar eclipse to exceed 7 minutes of totality, in over 800 years, is visible in the Pacific and Peru.
The Moscow Trial initiated on January 23 is concluded.
Leading Korean dancer Choi Seung-hee arrives in Le Havre, France after her tour in the United States.
Arising from The Munich Agreement, Hungary is "awarded" the Felvidek region of South Slovakia and Ruthenia.

Benito Mussolini and his Foreign Minister, Count Galeazzo Ciano, order "spontaneous" demonstrations in the Italian Chamber of Deputies, demanding that France cede Tunisia, Nice, Corsica and French Somaliland to Italy.
In the face of overwhelming Japanese military pressure, Chiang Kai-shek withdraws his government to Chungking.
The Imperial Japanese Army largely overruns Canton.
The Mauthausen concentration camp is built in Austria.
Adolf Hitler is Time magazine's "Man of the Year", as the most influential person of the year.
The European crisis over German demands for annexation of the Sudeten borderland of Czechoslovakia becomes increasingly severe.
Black Sunday at Bondi Beach, Sydney, Australia: 300 swimmers are dragged out to sea in 3 freak waves; 80 lifesavers save all but 5.
Lord Runciman is recalled to London from Prague, in order to brief the British government on the situation in the Sudetenland.
Sweden, Norway, and Finland refuse Germany's offer of non-aggression pacts.
A ceasefire ends the Battles of Khalkhin Gol, the undeclared border war between the Soviet Union (and Mongolian allies) and Japan.
Norway claims Queen Maud Land in Antarctica.
The first issue of Fashizmi is published in Tirana, Albania.
WWII: Diverse elements of the German Wehrmacht surround Warsaw, and demand its surrender.
The Einstein–Szilard letter is signed by Albert Einstein, advising President of the United States Franklin D. Roosevelt of the potential use of uranium to construct an atomic bomb.
Talks are completed in Ankara between French Ambassador René Massigli and Turkish Foreign Minister Şükrü Saracoğlu, resolving the Hatay dispute in Turkey's favor.
Mahatma Gandhi writes a personal letter to Adolf Hitler from India, addressing him as "My friend", requesting him to prevent any possible war.
WWII: Orzeł incident: Polish submarine ORP Orzeł escapes internment from Tallinn Harbour, Estonia, leading both the Soviet Union and Germany to question Estonia's neutrality.

The Hewlett-Packard technology and scientific instruments manufacturing company is founded by Bill Hewlett and David Packard, in a garage in Palo Alto, California, considered the birthplace of Silicon Valley.
Germany occupies Denmark and Norway in Operation Weserübung.
WWII: Paris is bombed by the Luftwaffe for the first time.
In Cambodia, the Khmer Issarak is formed to overthrow the French Army within the country.
Eleven British nationals, including Melville James Cox, are arrested on suspicion of spying for military intelligence by the secret police in Japan.
WWII: The Battle of Gabon, begun on October 27, concludes with Free French Forces taking control of the colony of Gabon and the remainder of French Equatorial Africa from the Vichy regime.
The German cruiser Admiral Hipper attacks a British shipping convoy (WS 5A) en route to Sierra Leone 700 miles (1,100 km) west of Cape Finisterre in Spain.
Albert Einstein gives a public address in the "I'm An American" series, on becoming an American citizen.

WWII: German auxiliary cruiser Komet shells and heavily damages the phosphate production facilities on the Pacific island of Nauru (under Australian protection at this time) while flying the Japanese flag.
Mahatma Gandhi, Indian spiritual non-violence leader, writes his second letter to Adolf Hitler, addressing him as "My friend", and requesting him to stop the war Germany had begun.
WWII: In response to Germany levelling Coventry 2 days before, the Royal Air Force begins to bomb Hamburg (by war's end, 50,000 Hamburg residents will have died from Allied attacks).

WWII: Australia, New Zealand, The Netherlands, the Free French, Yugoslavia, Costa Rica, Cuba, El Salvador, Guatemala and Honduras also officially declare war on Japan, and the Republic of China declares war on the Axis powers.
WWII: Hungary and Slovakia declare war on the Soviet Union.
The British Army's Special Air Service is formed.
The Political Warfare Executive is formed in the United Kingdom to disseminate propaganda to Germany and its occupied countries.
WWII: British troops attack Italian-held Eritrea in Africa.
Konrad Zuse presents the Z3, the world's first working programmable, fully automatic computer, in Berlin.
The Babi Yar massacre sees over 33,000 Jews killed by Nazi Einsatzgruppen near Kyiv.
WWII: Siege of Leningrad – German forces begin a siege against the Soviet Union's second-largest city, Leningrad.
A group of U.S. warships arrive in Auckland, New Zealand, on a goodwill visit.
The German–Turkish Treaty of Friendship is signed between Nazi Germany and Turkey, in Ankara.
WWII: Luxembourg is formally annexed to the German Reich.
Operation Pluto: The plan to construct oil pipelines under the English Channel, between England and France, is tested in the River Medway.

WWII: Doolittle Raid – Lieutenant Colonel Jimmy Doolittle leads a bombing mission against Japan, along with 79 other airmen of the U.S. Air Force, flying 16 North American B-25 Mitchell land-based bombers.
WWII: Battle of Madagascar (Operation Ironclad) begins when British forces land on the Vichy French colony of Madagascar.
The Holocaust: In Warsaw, two women, Zofia Kossak and Wanda Filipowicz, risk their lives by setting up the Council for the Assistance of the Jews.
WWII: Operation Blue: German forces of Army Group South under Generalfeldmarschall Fedor von Bock drive to Stalingrad and the Baku oil fields.
WWII: Guadalcanal campaign – The U.S. Navy and the U.S. Marine Corps start the first American offensive of the war, with an amphibious landing on the island of Guadalcanal in the Solomon Islands.
WWII: Marshalls–Gilberts raids: Admiral William Halsey Jr sends airstrikes from the carrier USS Enterprise against Kwajalein, Taroa, Wotje in the Marshall Islands.
The Holocaust: Dünamünde Action – 1,900 central European Jews are shot dead north east of Riga, 1,840 are killed on the 26th.
Cocoanut Grove fire: A fire in the Cocoanut Grove nightclub in Boston, Massachusetts, kills 491.
WWII: Khatyn massacre – The entire population of Khatyn, Belarus is burnt alive by German occupation forces.

The Holocaust: The last trainload of Jewish prisoners is moved from Bełżec extermination camp in occupied Poland (for gassing at Sobibór), and for the remainder of the year the Nazis make efforts to obliterate the site.
Exiled French aviator Antoine de Saint-Exupéry's self-illustrated children's novella, The Little Prince, is published in New York City, the all-time best-selling book originating in French.
WWII: Operation Longcloth: Chindit forces (some 3,000 men) of the 77th Indian Infantry Brigade under Brigadier General Orde Wingate cross the Chindwin River and proceed into Burma.
WWII: Admiral Karl Dönitz orders most U-boats to withdraw from the Atlantic Ocean.
Italian submarine Leonardo da Vinci sinks Canadian Pacific liner RMS Empress of Canada off Sierra Leone.
WWII: US landing at Nadzab: The 503rd Parachute Regiment under Colonel George Jones lands and occupies Nadzab, just east of the port city of Lae, in northeastern Papua New Guinea.
Banco Bradesco is founded in Marília, São Paulo, Brazil.
WWII: Landing at Amchitka: American forces make an unopposed landing on Amchitka, an island of the Aleutian Islands, southwest of Alaska.
John F. Kennedy and crew are found by Solomon Islands coastwatchers Biuku Gasa and Eroni Kumana, with their dugout canoe.
Belgium, Netherlands and Luxembourg constitute Benelux as representatives of the exiled governments sign the London Customs Convention.

Operation Bagration: A general attack by Soviet forces clears the German forces from Belarus, resulting in the destruction of German Army Group Centre, possibly the greatest defeat of the Wehrmacht during WWII.
Austrian-born economist Friedrich Hayek publishes his book The Road to Serfdom in London.
Rome falls to the Allies, the first of the Axis capitals to fall.
Jean-Paul Sartre's existentialist drama No Exit (Huis Clos) premières in Nazi-occupied Paris.
The Dutch famine ("Hongerwinter") begins, in the occupied northern part of the Netherlands.

Princess Charlotte Louise Juliette Louvet Grimaldi of Monaco, heir to the throne, resigns in favor of her son Prince Rainier Louis Henri Maxence Bertrand Grimaldi, who later reigns as Prince Rainier III of Monaco.
WWII: Partisan troops of the National Liberation Movement enter Tirana, the capital of Albania.
The Holocaust: Polish insurgents liberate a German labor camp in Warsaw, freeing 348 Jewish prisoners.
The original stage version of The Glass Menagerie by Tennessee Williams premieres in Chicago.

The United Nations is founded by ratification of its Charter, by 29 nations including the United Kingdom, the United States, France, Canada, Egypt, Brazil, Haiti, Luxembourg, the Soviet Union, Czechoslovakia and others.
The Yalta Conference unites Winston Churchill, Franklin D. Roosevelt, and Joseph Stalin to shape postwar Europe and establish the United Nations.
Paris marks the first anniversary of its liberation.
General Alexander Löhr, Commander of German Army Group E near Topolšica, Slovenia, signs the capitulation of German occupation troops.
Raymond L. Libby of American Cyanamid's research laboratories, at Stamford, Connecticut, announces a method of orally administering the antibiotic penicillin.
Arthur C. Clarke puts forward the idea of a geosynchronous communications satellite, in a Wireless World magazine article.
WWII: The U.S. Ninth Army under General William H. Simpson crosses the Elbe River astride Magdeburg, and reaches Tangermünde — only 50 miles from Berlin.
Uruguay declares war on Germany and Japan.
Mongolians vote for independence from China.
WWII: The Soviet Union occupies Warsaw, Poland.
Cathay Pacific Airways is founded in Hong Kong, by American Roy Farrell and Australian Sydney de Kantzow.

ENIAC (for "Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer"), an early general-purpose electronic computer, is unveiled at the University of Pennsylvania; it weighs 60,000 pounds (over 27 tons), and occupies a big room.
The Central All-Indonesian Workers Organization (SOBSI) is founded in Jakarta.
At Club 500 in Atlantic City, New Jersey, Dean Martin and Jerry Lewis stage their first show as a comedy team.
In the last mass lynching in the United States, a mob of white men shoot and kill two African-American couples, near Moore's Ford Bridge in Georgia.
Japanese Lt. General Masaharu Homma is executed outside Manila in the Philippines, for leading the Bataan Death March.
French Guiana, Guadeloupe, Martinique and Réunion become overseas départements of France.
The Winecoff Hotel fire in Atlanta, United States, kills 119.
John Peters Humphrey, main author of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, becomes Director of the United Nations Division of Human Rights.
The Havana Conference begins between U.S. organized crime bosses in Havana, Cuba.
The Doomsday Clock of the Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists is introduced.
First recorded use of the word computer in its modern sense, referring to an electronic digital machine.
The previous discovery of the 'Dead Sea Scrolls' in the Qumran Caves (above the northwest shore of the Dead Sea) by Bedouin shepherds, becomes known.
A rebellion against French rule erupts in Madagascar.
The Arab Ba'ath Party is established by merger in Damascus.
Kenneth Arnold makes the first widely reported UFO sighting near Mount Rainier, Washington.
The United Nations Conference on Trade and Employment begins in Havana, Cuba.
Portella della Ginestra massacre: The Salvatore Giuliano gang of Sicilian separatists opens fire on a Labour Day parade at Portella della Ginestra, Sicily, killing 11 people and wounding 27.
The arrest of four steel workers in Marseille begins a French communist riot, that also spreads to Paris.
President Harry S. Truman delivers the first televised White House address, speaking on the world food crises.
Children's Bargain Town, a predecessor of toy and child-related retailer Toys "R" Us, is founded in Washington, D.C., United States.
The RAND Corporation is established, as an independent nonprofit policy research and analysis institution, in the United States.
Toho strikes: A sitdown strike at Toho film studio in Tokyo ends after the studio is surrounded by 2,000 police and a platoon of U.S. Eighth Army soldiers.
Liberal politician Jorge Eliécer Gaitán's assassination provokes a violent riot in Bogotá (the Bogotazo) and a further 10 years of violence (La Violencia) across Colombia.
José Figueres Ferrer abolishes the army in Costa Rica, making it the first country in history to do so.
Assassination of Mahatma Gandhi: Indian pacifist and leader Mahatma Gandhi is shot by Nathuram Godse in New Delhi.
Brandeis University is formally founded in Massachusetts.
Margaret Chase Smith of Maine is elected United States Senator, becoming the first woman to serve in both the U.S. House of Representatives and the United States Senate.
First National Games of Pakistan held in Karachi.
The American Broadcasting Company (otherwise known as ABC) begins television services, on WFIL-TV in Philadelphia (later WPVI-TV).
The former British colony of Newfoundland joins Canada, as its 10th province.
Rainier III becomes Prince of Monaco, upon the death of his maternal grandfather Louis II.
Deportivo Saprissa enters Costa Rican soccer's first division.
Nereid, a moon of Neptune, is discovered by Gerard Kuiper.
With the passage of the Bodh Gaya Temple Act by the Indian government, Mahabodhi Temple is restored to partial Buddhist control.
The second trial of Alger Hiss for perjury begins in New York, again with Whittaker Chambers as principal witness.
Nathuram Godse and Narayan Apte are executed for assassinating Mahatma Gandhi.
Oil is discovered beneath the Caspian Sea, off the coast of the Azerbaijan Soviet Socialist Republic.
The Republic of Ireland formally becomes a republic, and leaves the British Commonwealth.
Mao Zedong proclaims the People's Republic of China, ending the Chinese Civil War and establishing communist rule.
Rede Tupi, the first television broadcast network in South America, is founded in Brazil.
Albert Einstein warns that nuclear war could lead to mutual destruction.
A phenomenal winter storm ravages the northeastern United States, brings 30–50 inches of snow and temperatures below zero, and kills 323 people.
In Wheeling, West Virginia, Senator Joseph McCarthy of Wisconsin makes a speech that claims to have 205 communists in the U.S. State Department.
In West Virginia, 372,000 coal miners strike (they remain out until March 3).
India promulgates its constitution, forming a republic, and Rajendra Prasad is sworn in as its first president.
The President of Venezuela, Colonel Carlos Delgado Chalbaud, is kidnapped and murdered in Caracas.
Acting President of the Republic of China Li Zongren ends his term in office and Chiang Kai-shek resumes his duties as president, after moving the government of the Republic to Taipei, Taiwan.
Egypt demands that Britain remove all its troops from the Suez Canal zone.

In his encyclical Humani generis, Pope Pius XII requires Catholic theologians to defer to the teachings of the Church as a whole but declares evolution to be a serious hypothesis that does not contradict essential Catholic views.
A formal peace agreement between Canada and Germany is signed.
The Convention People's Party wins national elections in Gold Coast (British colony).
An 18-year-old sailor is fined for kissing in public in Stockholm, Sweden.
The first Pan American Games open in Buenos Aires.
The cremated remains of Mary Reeser are found at her home in Saint Petersburg, Florida.
July 1 – In New Mexico, Arizona, California, Oregon, Washington and British Columbia, thousands of acres of forests are destroyed in fires.
Charlotte Whitton becomes mayor of Ottawa and Canada's first woman mayor of a major city.
Desert Rock exercises, the first military exercises for nuclear war, with infantry troops included, are held in the Nevada desert.
Operation Greenhouse: The first thermonuclear weapon is tested in the "George" test on Enewetok Atoll in the Marshall Islands by the United States.
Experimental Breeder Reactor I (EBR-1), the world's first (experimental) nuclear power plant, opens in Idaho, United States.

Princess Elizabeth, Duchess of Edinburgh, becomes monarch of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland and the British Dominions: Canada, Australia, New Zealand, South Africa, Pakistan and Ceylon.
Reparation negotiations between West Germany and Israel end in Luxembourg: Germany will pay 3 billion Deutsche Marks.
Al Arabi sports and association football club is founded in Qatar.
During the Mau Mau Uprising, the poisonous latex of the African milk bush is used to kill cattle, in an incident of Biological warfare.
Alain Bombard begins to sail from the Canary Islands to Barbados in 65 days without using provisions; he reaches them December 23.
Farouk of Egypt has himself announced as a descendant of the Islamic prophet, Muhammad.
Navigation opens on the Volga–Don Canal, connecting the Caspian Sea basin with that of the Black Sea.
West Ice accidents: During a severe storm in the West Ice, east of Greenland, 78 seal hunters on 5 Norwegian seal hunting vessels vanish without a trace.
One of the first successful gender-affirming surgeries is performed in Copenhagen on Christine Jorgensen.
The first successful surgical separation of conjoined twins is conducted in Mount Sinai Hospital, Cleveland, Ohio.
The UNIVAC 1103 is the first commercial computer to use random-access memory.
Estonian émigrés found a government-in-exile in Oslo.
Georgia approves the first literature censorship board in the United States.
The first ascent of Nanga Parbat in the Pakistan Himalayas, the world's ninth highest mountain, is made by Austrian climber Hermann Buhl alone on a German–Austrian expedition.
Francis Crick and James Watson publish "Molecular Structure of Nucleic Acids: A Structure for Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid", their description of the double helix structure of DNA.
The French government ousts King Mohammed V of Morocco, and exiles him to Corsica.

Alto Broadcasting System (ABS) in the Philippines makes the first television broadcast in southeast Asia, through DZAQ-TV. Alto Broadcasting System is the predecessor of what will later become ABS-CBN Corporation.
Uprising in Plzeň: Currency reform causes riots in Czechoslovakia.
Operation Big Switch: Prisoners of war are repatriated to the United States after the Korean War.
Joseph Stalin suffers a stroke, after an all-night dinner with Soviet Union interior minister Lavrentiy Beria and future premiers Georgy Malenkov, Nikolai Bulganin, and Nikita Khrushchev.
The modern form of value-added tax is first implemented by Maurice Lauré, joint director of the French tax authority, in France's Ivory Coast colony.
A CIA-engineered military coup occurs in Guatemala.
SEATO is established in Bangkok, Thailand.
Joey Giardello knocks out Willie Tory at Madison Square Garden in the first televised boxing prize fight to be shown in colour.
The U.S. Congress and President Dwight D. Eisenhower authorize the founding of the United States Air Force Academy in Colorado.
The Castle Romeo nuclear test explosion is executed at Bikini Atoll, in the Marshall Islands.
The first mass vaccination of children against polio begins in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, United States.
A fire on board the U.S. Navy aircraft carrier USS Bennington, off Narragansett Bay, Massachusetts, kills 103 sailors.
Red Scare: The United States Senate votes 67–22 to censure Wisconsin Senator Joseph McCarthy, for "conduct that tends to bring the Senate into dishonor and disrepute.".
Hurricane Hazel makes U.S. landfall; it is the only recorded Category 4 hurricane to strike as far north as North Carolina.
The International Federation of Blood Donor Organizations is founded in Luxembourg.
José Ramón Guizado becomes president of Panama.
El Al Flight 402 from Vienna (Austria) to Tel Aviv, via Istanbul, is shot down over Bulgaria.
The Southeast Asia Treaty Organization (SEATO) is established, at a meeting in Bangkok.
Cardiff is officially declared capital of Wales by the British Government.
Joe Brown and George Band are the first to climb Kangchenjunga in the Himalayas, as part of the British Kangchenjunga expedition led by Charles Evans.
The Montgomery Improvement Association is formed in Montgomery, Alabama, by Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., and other Black ministers to coordinate the Montgomery bus boycott by Black people.
Australian comedian Barry Humphries first introduces his character Edna Everage on stage in Melbourne.
Nearly 100 die in a fire at a home for the elderly in Yokohama, Japan.
Mir mine, the first diamond mine in the Soviet Union, is discovered.
Vyacheslav Molotov resigns as foreign minister of the Soviet Union; he later becomes ambassador to Mongolia.
The British deport Archbishop Makarios from Cyprus to the Seychelles.
Dalit Buddhist movement (India): B. R. Ambedkar, Dalit leader, converts to Buddhism, along with 500,000 followers.
The Hungarian Revolution breaks out against the pro-Soviet government, originating as a student demonstration in Budapest.
Fidel Castro and Che Guevara depart from Tuxpan, Veracruz, Mexico, en route to Santiago de Cuba aboard the yacht Granma, with 82 men.
British and French troops leave the Suez Canal region.
In Yugoslavia, former prime minister Milovan Đilas is arrested after he criticizes Josip Broz Tito.
A United States Navy team becomes the third group to reach the South Pole (arriving by air), and commences construction of the first permanent Amundsen–Scott South Pole Station.
Trans-Canada Air Lines Flight 810, a Canadair North Star, crashes into Slesse Mountain near Chilliwack, British Columbia.
At age 48, Dutch boxer Bep van Klaveren contests his last match in Rotterdam.
IBM sells the first compiler for the Fortran scientific programming language.
The Treaty of Rome (Patto di Roma) establishes the European Economic Community (EEC; predecessor of the European Union) between Italy, France, West Germany, Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg.
Sputnik program: The Soviet Union launches Sputnik 2, with the first animal to orbit the Earth, a dog named Laika, on board.
Arturo Lezama becomes President of the National Council of Government of Uruguay.
Zodi Ikhia founds the Nigerien Democratic Front (FDN) in Niger.
A United States Air Force Boeing C-97 disappears somewhere over the Pacific Ocean near the coast of Japan.
Raja Fashions, a tailoring business, is founded in Hong Kong.
The Ibirapuera Planetarium (the first in the Southern Hemisphere) is inaugurated in the city of São Paulo, Brazil.
Indonesian president Sukarno survives a grenade attack at the Cikini School in Jakarta, but several children are killed.
The Mackinac Bridge, the world's longest suspension bridge between anchorages at this time, opens in the United States, to connect Michigan's two peninsulas.
Soviet polar pilot V. M. Perov on Li-2 rescues four Belgian polar explorers, led by Gaston de Gerlache, who have survived a plane crash in Antarctica 250 km from their base five days earlier.
A general strike is called in Paraguay.
Chad, the Republic of the Congo and Gabon become autonomous republics within the French colonial empire.
Guinea declares itself independent from France, rejecting that nation's new constitution.
The Guatemalan Air Force fires on Mexican fishing boats which had strayed into Guatemalan territory, triggering the Mexico–Guatemala conflict.
Australian athlete Herb Elliott clips almost 3 seconds off the world record for the mile run at Santry Stadium, Dublin, recording a time of 3 minutes 54.5 seconds.
October 15 – Illinois observes the centennial of the Lincoln–Douglas debates.
Crisis in France: French Algerian protesters seize government offices in Algiers, leading to a military coup.
During a visit to Caracas, Venezuela, Vice President Richard Nixon's car is attacked by anti-American demonstrators.
Battle of Santa Clara: Rebel troops under Camilo Cienfuegos and Che Guevara begin to invade Santa Clara, Cuba.
The first skull of Australopithecus is discovered by Louis Leakey and his wife Mary in the Olduvai Gorge of Tanzania.
The Confédération Mondiale des Activités Subaquatiques is founded in Monaco.
In Laos the Laotian Civil War begins between the Kingdom of Laos and communist rebels, the Pathet Lao.
The Workers' Stadium sports venue in Beijing (China) is officially opened.
In Rwanda, Hutu politician Dominique Mbonyumutwa is beaten up by Tutsi forces, leading to a period of violence known as the wind of destruction.
The southernmost island of the Maldives archipelago, Addu Atoll, declares its independence from the Kingdom of the Maldives, initiating the United Suvadive Republic.
Alaska is admitted as the 49th U.S. state.
Hawaii is admitted as the 50th and last U.S. state.
Wing Commander Michael Beetham flying a British Royal Air Force Vickers Valiant sets a record of 11 hours 27 minutes for a non-stop London-Cape Town flight.
National People's Congress elects Liu Shaoqi as Chairman of the People's Republic of China, as a successor of Mao Zedong.
The first international Summer Paralympics open in Rome under the title "9th International Stoke Mandeville Games", the first quadrennial paralympic event outside of England.
The African and Malagasy Organisation for Economic Cooperation (OAMCE – Organisation Africain et Malagache de Coopération Économique) is established.
The Malagasy Republic (Madagascar) becomes independent from France.
Upper Volta (modern-day Burkina Faso) becomes independent from France.
Cameroon becomes independent from France.
The Ivory Coast becomes independent from France.
Dahomey (modern-day Benin) becomes independent from France.
Mali, the sole remaining member of the "Mali Federation" (following the withdrawal of Senegal one month earlier), declares its full independence as the Republic of Mali.
Mauritania becomes independent of France.
Niger becomes independent from France.
Luxembourg's national holiday, the Grand Duke's Official Birthday, is set on June 23 by Grand Ducal decree.
April – Drilling for Project Mohole is undertaken off the coast of Guadalupe Island, Mexico.
The United States founds the Alliance for Progress.
Mongolia and Mauritania join the United Nations.

Unification Day (Cameroon): The formerly British Southern Cameroons gains independence from the United Kingdom by vote of the UN General Assembly and joins with formerly French Cameroun to form the Federal Republic of Cameroon.

Tunku Abdul Rahman, Prime Minister of Malaya, holds a press conference in Singapore, announcing his idea to form the Federation of Malaysia, comprising Malaya, Singapore, Sarawak, Brunei and North Borneo (Sabah).
Following a four-day conference in Casablanca, five African chiefs of state announce plans for a NATO-type African organization to ensure common defense.
The Arab League takes over protecting Kuwait; the last British troops leave.
Sierra Leone becomes independent from the United Kingdom.
Hurricane Hattie devastates Belize City, Belize killing over 270. After the hurricane, the capital moves to the inland city of Belmopan.
Norway launches its 1st sounding rocket, Ferdinand 1, from Andøya Space Center and becomes a space nation.
Air France Flight 007 (a Boeing 707) crashes on take-off at Orly Airport in Paris; 130 of 132 people on board are killed, 2 flight attendants survive.
Western Samoa becomes independent from New Zealand.
Tanganyika (modern-day Tanzania) becomes a republic within the Commonwealth of Nations, with Julius Nyerere as president.
The North Kalimantan National Army revolts in Brunei, in the first stirrings of the Indonesian Confrontation.
Rwanda and Burundi gain full independence from Belgium.
Flying Tiger Line Flight 923, a Lockheed L-1049H Super Constellation registered as N6923C, ditched into the Atlantic Ocean killing 28 occupants out of 76 on board.
Britain acknowledges the right of Nyasaland (modern-day Malawi) to secede from the Central African Federation.

The Caribbean island of Jamaica becomes independent of the United Kingdom's British Empire and is the first English speaking-sovereign country in the West Indies and is first part of the Commonwealth of Nations.
Anti-apartheid activist Nelson Mandela is arrested by the South African government near Howick, and charged with incitement to rebellion.
An earthquake in Skopje, Yugoslavia (present-day North Macedonia) leaves 1,800 dead.
The Le Monde Theater fire in Dioirbel, Senegal, kills 64 people.
A smallpox outbreak hits Stockholm, Sweden, lasting until July.
David H. Frisch and J.H. Smith prove that the radioactive decay of mesons is slowed by their motion (see Einstein's special relativity and general relativity).
Rioters burn down the British Embassy in Jakarta, to protest the formation of Malaysia.
Martin Luther King Jr. delivers his "I Have a Dream" speech on the steps of the Lincoln Memorial to an audience of at least 250,000, during the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom.
Nigeria becomes a republic; The 1st Republican Constitution is established.
Arecibo Observatory, a radio telescope, officially begins operation in Puerto Rico.
Pope Paul VI (Giovanni Battista Montini) succeeds Pope John XXIII as the 262nd pope.
John F. Kennedy gives his "Ich bin ein Berliner" speech in West Berlin, Germany.
Tanganyika and Zanzibar merge to form Tanzania.
In Laos, the coalition government of Prince Souvanna Phouma is deposed by a right-wing military group, led by Brig.
Northern Rhodesia, a former British protectorate, becomes the independent Republic of Zambia, ending 73 years of British rule.
The United Nations Security Council adopts by a 9–0 vote a resolution deploring a British air attack on a fort in Yemen 12 days earlier, in which 25 persons were reported killed.
The National Movement of the Revolution is established in the Republic of the Congo, becoming the country's sole legal political party.

At 4:00 a.m., John George Kemeny and Thomas Eugene Kurtz run the first computer program written in BASIC (Beginners' All-purpose Symbolic Instruction Code), an easy to learn high level programming language which they have created.
Malawi receives its independence from the United Kingdom.
Nelson Mandela and 7 others are sentenced to life imprisonment in South Africa, and sent to the Robben Island prison.
Vietnam War: At a rally in Saigon, South Vietnamese Prime Minister and military leader Nguyễn Khánh calls for expanding the war into North Vietnam.
Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. is awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in Oslo, Norway.
The Intelsat I ("Early Bird") communications satellite is launched.
In Rhodesia (modern-day Zimbabwe), the white-minority government of Ian Smith unilaterally declares de facto independence ('UDI').
President Kenneth Kaunda of Zambia announces that Zambia and the United Kingdom have agreed on a deadline before which the Rhodesian white government should be ousted.
The Yemeni Nasserist Unionist People's Organisation is founded in Ta'izz.
The Gambia becomes independent from the United Kingdom.
Gambia, Maldives and Singapore are admitted as members of the United Nations.
A Charlie Brown Christmas, the first Peanuts television special, debuts on CBS in the United States.
A trolleybus plunges into the Nile at Cairo, Egypt, killing 74 passengers.
An explosion at an Arkansas missile plant kills 53.
Police in Algiers break up demonstrations by people who have taken to the streets chanting slogans in support of deposed President Ahmed Ben Bella.
Lesotho and Botswana are admitted to the United Nations.
Zambia threatens to leave the Commonwealth of Nations because of British peace overtures to Rhodesia.
Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Republic begin negotiations in Kuwait to end the war in Yemen.
A new government is formed in the Republic of the Congo, led by Ambroise Noumazalaye.
Kwame Nkrumah arrives in Guinea and is granted asylum.
The International Court of Justice rules in favour of South Africa in a case on the administration of South West Africa which has been brought before them by Ethiopia and Liberia.
British Guiana achieves independence from the United Kingdom, becoming Guyana.
Haile Selassie visits Jamaica for the first time, meeting with Rasta leaders.
Basutoland becomes independent of the United Kingdom and takes the name Lesotho.
Barbados achieves independence from the United Kingdom.
A Soviet nuclear test is conducted at the Semipalatinsk Test Site, Eastern Kazakhstan.
Omar Ali Saifuddin III of Brunei abdicates in favour of his son, His Majesty Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah.
A military coup occurs in Togo under the leadership of Étienne Eyadema.
The People's Republic of South Yemen becomes independent of the United Kingdom.
General Anastasio Somoza Debayle becomes president of Nicaragua.
Venera program: Venera 4 is launched by the Soviet Union (the first space probe to analyze another planet's atmosphere and successfully return data).
Donald Sangster becomes the new prime minister of Jamaica, succeeding Alexander Bustamante.
American researchers discover the Madrid Codices by Leonardo da Vinci in the National Library of Spain.
The largest-ever blizzard to hit the US city of Chicago begins.
Major floods hit Lisbon, Portugal, killing 462.
Vietnam War: Operation Commando Hunt is initiated to interdict men and supplies on the Ho Chi Minh trail, through Laos into South Vietnam.
In Mali, President Modibo Keïta's regime is overthrown in a bloodless military coup led by Moussa Traoré.
In Panama, a military coup d'état, led by Col. Boris Martinez and Col. Omar Torrijos, overthrows the democratically elected (but highly controversial) government of President Arnulfo Arias.
Arenal Volcano erupts in Costa Rica for the first time in centuries.
CARIFTA, the Caribbean Free Trade Association, is formally created as an agreement between Antigua and Barbuda, Barbados, Guyana, and Trinidad and Tobago.
Equatorial Guinea receives its independence from Spain.
A second republic is declared in the Maldives.
Mauritius achieves independence from British rule.
Puerta 12 tragedy: A football stampede in Buenos Aires leaves 74 dead and 150 injured.
Nauru president Hammer DeRoburt declares independence from Australia, Britain and New Zealand.
Common African, Malagasy and Mauritian Organization (OCAMM) (Organisation Commune Africaine Malgache et Mauricienne) is established.
An American teenager known as 'Robert R.' dies in St. Louis, Missouri, United States, of a baffling medical condition.
Apollo program: The Apollo 12 spacecraft splashes down safely in the Pacific Ocean, ending the second crewed mission to the Moon.
Football War: After Honduras loses an association football match against El Salvador, rioting breaks out in Honduras against Salvadoran migrant workers.
The first ARPANET link is established (the progenitor of the global Internet).
A 1.2 megaton thermonuclear device is tested at Amchitka Island, Alaska.
An explosion aboard the aircraft carrier USS Enterprise near Hawaii kills 28 and injures 314.
Fourteen men, 9 of them Jews, are executed in Baghdad for spying for Israel.
Chappaquiddick incident: US Senator Edward M. Kennedy drives off a bridge into a tidal pond after leaving a party on Chappaquiddick Island, Massachusetts, killing Mary Jo Kopechne.
The Piazza Fontana bombing in Milan, Italy, kills 17 people and injures 88.
Richard Nixon begins a tour of Europe, visiting Italy, Yugoslavia, Spain, the United Kingdom and Republic of Ireland.
Citroën introduces the Citroën SM, the world's fastest front-wheel drive auto at this time, at the annual Geneva Motor Show in Switzerland.
In Berlin, Red Army Faction members rob three banks, with loot totaling over DM 200,000.
The Soviet Union enters the International Civil Aviation Organization, after having resisted joining the UN Agency for more than 25 years.
Guinea recognizes the German Democratic Republic.
National Democratic Front for the Liberation of Oman and the Arabian Gulf guerrillas attack military garrisons at Izki and Nizwa in Oman.
Guyana becomes a Republic within the Commonwealth of Nations.
Thor Heyerdahl's papyrus boat Ra II arrives in Barbados.
All 57 men aboard the French submarine Eurydice are killed when the vessel implodes while making a practice dive in the Mediterranean Sea.
Vietnam War: U.S. President Richard Nixon announces that the United States will withdraw 40,000 more troops before Christmas.
Jim Morrison, lead singer of The Doors, dies of a heart failure at the age of 27 in the bathtub of his apartment on the 3rd floor of the Rue Beautreillis 17 in Paris, France.
Border clashes occur between Tanzania and Uganda.
Madagascar accuses the U.S. of conspiring to oust the government; the U.S. recalls its ambassador.
A right-wing coup attempt is exposed in Laos.
Tupamaros kidnap Geoffrey Jackson, British ambassador to Uruguay, in Montevideo, keeping him captive until September.
Qatar gains independence from the United Kingdom.
Seventy Brazilian political prisoners are released in Santiago, Chile; Giovanni Enrico Bucher is released January 16.
Siaka Stevens is sworn in as the first president of Sierra Leone.
Hastings Banda is proclaimed President for Life of Malawi.
Oman gains independence from the United Kingdom.
In Somalia, the government of President Siad Barre formally introduces the Somali alphabet as the country's official writing script.
A coup in the Republic of Dahomey (later Benin) led by Mathieu Kérékou removes a civilian government (which has been headed by a triumvirate consisting of Ahomadégbé, Apithy and Maga).
Jigme Singye Wangchuck succeeds his father Jigme Dorji Wangchuck as King of Bhutan.
President of Ecuador José María Velasco Ibarra is deposed for the fourth time.
Ikiza: Burundi government forces begin a 4-month genocide against the Hutu people, killing 100,000–300,000.

The Canadian ketch Vega, flying the Greenpeace III banner, collides with the French naval minesweeper La Paimpolaise while in international waters to protest French nuclear weapon tests in the South Pacific.
The Pioneer 10 spacecraft is launched from Cape Kennedy, to be the first man-made spacecraft to leave the Solar System.
The Libertarian enclave Minerva on a platform in the South Pacific, sponsored by the Phoenix Foundation, declares independence.
Fire at the Sunshine Mine, a silver mine in Idaho, kills 91.
In St. Peter's Basilica (Vatican City), Laszlo Toth attacks Michelangelo's Pietà statue with a geologist's hammer, shouting that he is Jesus Christ.
Luís Cabral declares the independence of the Republic of Guinea-Bissau from the Estado Novo regime in Portugal.
The United Kingdom, the Republic of Ireland, and Denmark enter the European Economic Community, which later becomes the European Union.
A military insurrection in Uruguay poses an institutional challenge to President Juan María Bordaberry.
Queen Sisowath Kossamak of Cambodia is released from house arrest to Beijing.
The Avianca Building in Bogotá, Colombia, suffers a serious fire, in which four people are killed.
The United Nations recognizes the independence of Guinea-Bissau.
Pioneer 11 is launched on a mission to study the Solar System.
Pioneer program: Pioneer 10 sends back the first close-up images of Jupiter.
Papua New Guinea gains self-government from Australia.
The Bosphorus Bridge in Istanbul, Turkey, is completed, connecting the continents of Europe and Asia over the Bosphorus Strait for the first time in history.
Greece withdraws its forces from NATO's military command structure, as a result of the Turkish invasion of Cyprus.
African Youth Amílcar Cabral is founded in Guinea-Bissau.
Fire breaks out in the Joelma Building in São Paulo, Brazil; 177 die, 293 are injured, 11 die later of their injuries.
Lufthansa Flight 540 crashes in Nairobi, Kenya, due to a mechanical failure, killing 59 of its 157 occupants.
Carnation Revolution: A left-wing military coup in Portugal restores democracy, ending 41 years of the Estado Novo dictatorship in the country.
The Troubles: The Dublin and Monaghan bombings are carried out by the Ulster Volunteer Force, when they explode four car bombs in counties Dublin and Monaghan in the Republic of Ireland.
An express train bound for Germany from Belgrade derails in Zagreb, Yugoslavia (now Croatia), killing more than 150 passengers.
Kuala Lumpur, the capital of Malaysia, is declared a Federal Territory.
The Terracotta Army of Qin Shi Huang is discovered at Xi'an, China.
Arecibo message: The radio telescope at the Arecibo Observatory on Puerto Rico sends an interstellar radio message towards Messier 13, the Great Globular Cluster in Hercules.
A failed military coup d'état by far-left activists occurs in Portugal.
After a referendum and seven years of military rule, modern-day Greece is established as the Hellenic Republic.
Colonel Richard Ratsimandrava, President of Madagascar, is assassinated.

In Laos, the Second Indochina War ends, when the communist party of the Pathet Lao takes over Vientiane and defeats the Kingdom of Laos, forcing King Sisavang Vatthana to abdicate and creating the Lao People's Democratic Republic.
The National Assembly of Senegal passes a law that will pave way for a multi-party system (albeit highly restricted).
The first Cuban forces arrive in Angola to join Soviet personnel who are there to assist the MPLA that controls less than a quarter of Angolan territory.
In Lomé, Togo, the European Economic Community and 46 African, Caribbean and Pacific countries sign a financial and economic treaty, known as the first Lomé Convention.
Cape Verde, Mozambique and São Tomé and Príncipe join the United Nations.
Cape Verde gains independence after 500 years of Portuguese rule.
Suriname gains independence from the Kingdom of the Netherlands.

The Cray-1, the first commercially developed supercomputer, is released by Seymour Cray's Cray Research, with the first purchaser being the Energy Research and Development Administration (ERDA) in Los Alamos, New Mexico.
The Senegalese political party PAI-Rénovation is legally recognized, becoming the third legal party in the country.
Chairman of the Chinese Communist Party Mao Zedong dies in Beijing after a series of heart attacks.
The Body Shop, the retail chain for skin care products and cosmetics founded by Anita Roddick, opens its first branch in Brighton, England.
The Selous Scouts of the Rhodesian Army conduct a cross-border raid into Nyadzonya, Mozambique in Operation Eland, an action that led to severe political and diplomatic consequences on Rhodesia.
In Santiago, Chile, Cruzeiro from Brazil beats River Plate from Argentina and are the Copa Libertadores de América champions in Association football.
The world's first known case of Ebola is recorded in Nzara, Sudan (now South Sudan).
Seychelles gains independence from the United Kingdom.
Trinidad and Tobago becomes a republic, replacing Elizabeth II as its head of state with President Ellis Clarke.
The New Jersey Supreme Court rules that patient in a persistent vegetative state in the Karen Ann Quinlan case can be disconnected from her ventilator.
Three bombs explode in Moscow within 37 minutes, killing seven.
The National Assembly of Quebec passes the Charter of the French Language (Law 101, La charte de la langue française) making French the official language of the Canadian province of Quebec.
An IAS Cargo Boeing 707 airplane crash in Lusaka, Zambia, kills all six on board.
Djibouti and Vietnam join the United Nations.
Torrijos-Carter treaties: Treaties between Panama and the United States on the status of the Panama Canal are signed.
Under pressure from the Carter Administration, President of Nicaragua Anastasio Somoza Debayle lifts the state of siege in Nicaragua.
Óscar Romero, an outspoken opponent of violence, becomes Archbishop of San Salvador, El Salvador.
A bloodless coup installs France-Albert René as President of the Seychelles.
The Taksim Square massacre in Istanbul results in 34 deaths and hundreds of injuries.
The TCP/IP test succeeds, connecting 3 ARPANET nodes (of 111), in what eventually becomes the Internet protocol.
Rhodesian Bush War: Rhodesia attacks Zambia.
Pedro Joaquín Chamorro Cardenal, a critic of the Nicaraguan government, is assassinated; riots erupt against Somoza's government.
In Guyana, Jim Jones leads his Peoples Temple cult in a mass murder–suicide in his commune, Jonestown, that claims 918 lives in all, 909 of them at Jonestown itself, including over 270 children.
Ali Soilih is found dead in the Comoros, allegedly shot when trying to escape.
The People's Republic of China lifts a ban on works by Aristotle, William Shakespeare and Charles Dickens.
Dominica gains its independence from the United Kingdom.
Norway opens a natural gas field, in the Polar Sea.
Tuvalu becomes independent from the United Kingdom.
Charon, a satellite of Pluto, is discovered.
Iranian Army troops open fire on rioters in Tehran, killing 122, wounding over 200.
Michael Jackson releases his breakthrough album Off the Wall.
Uganda–Tanzania War: Battle of Lira: Tanzania and its Uganda National Liberation Front allies capture Lira, Uganda, from the forces of Ugandan dictator Idi Amin.
The Polisario Front signs a peace treaty with Mauritania.
A Nicaraguan National Guard soldier kills ABC TV news correspondent Bill Stewart and his interpreter Juan Espinosa.
A suspected gas explosion in a Warsaw bank kills 49 people.
Dictator Francisco Macías Nguema of Equatorial Guinea is overthrown in a bloody coup d'état led by Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo.
Pluto moves inside Neptune's orbit for the first time since either was known to science.
The Gilbert Islands become fully independent of the United Kingdom as Kiribati.
Maurice Bishop leads a successful coup in Grenada.
Greenland is granted limited autonomy from Denmark, with its own Parliament sitting in Nuuk.
Robert Mugabe is elected Prime Minister of Zimbabwe.
LOT Polish Airlines Flight 007 crashes during an emergency landing near Warsaw, Poland, killing a 14-man American boxing team and 73 others.
A coup in Suriname ousts the government of Henck Arron; leaders Dési Bouterse and Roy Horb replace it with a National Military Council.
Burning of the Spanish Embassy in Guatemala: The Spanish Embassy in Guatemala is invaded and set on fire, killing 36 people.
The Voyager 1 probe confirms the existence of Janus, a moon of Saturn.

A missionary (Jean Donovan) and three Roman Catholic nuns (Maura Clarke, Ita Ford, Dorothy Kazel), all Americans, are murdered by a military death squad in El Salvador while doing charity work during that country's civil war.
Apartheid: The African National Congress in South Africa publishes a statement by their imprisoned leader Nelson Mandela.
Rede Tupi, a Brazillian television channel in São Paulo, stopped broadcasting.
In Vanuatu, followers of John Frum's cargo cult on the island of Tanna declare secession as the nation of Tafea.
Canadian Caper: Six United States diplomats, posing as Canadians, manage to escape from Tehran, Iran, as they board a flight to Zürich, Switzerland, on Swissair.
Greece enters the European Economic Community, predecessor of the European Union.
In Riyadh, the Gulf Cooperation Council is created among Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates.
Belize, formerly British Honduras, gains its independence from the United Kingdom.

Iran–Contra affair: U.S. President Ronald Reagan signs the top secret National Security Decision Directive 17 (NSDD-17), authorizing the Central Intelligence Agency to recruit and support Contra rebels in Nicaragua.
Rotary International charters the Rotary Club of Grand Baie, Mauritius.
El Mozote massacre: In El Salvador, army units kill 900 civilians.
Antigua and Barbuda gains independence from the United Kingdom.
Palau becomes a self-governing territory.
The overcrowded ferry boat Sobral Santos II capsizes in the Amazon River, Óbidos, Brazil, killing at least 300 people.
The Jamaican reggae singer Bob Marley dies at age 36 from cancer.
Michael Jackson releases his sixth studio album, Thriller, in the United States, which will go on to be the best-selling album of all time.
Paul Biya becomes the second president of Cameroon following the resignation of Ahmadou Ahidjo.
Senegal and The Gambia form a loose Senegambia Confederation.
The first U.S. execution by lethal injection is carried out in Texas.
An Ethiopian Air Force Antonov An-26 with an unknown registration crashed near Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, killing all 73 occupants on board.
Argentine scrap metal workers (infiltrated by marines) raise the flag of Argentina on South Georgia and the Falkland Islands, two British overseas territories.
The United States places an embargo on Libyan oil imports, alleging Libyan state-sponsored terrorism.
The leader of Poland's outlawed Solidarity movement, Lech Wałęsa, is released from 11 months of internment near the Soviet border.
Swedish pop group ABBA make their final public performance on the British TV programme The Late, Late Breakfast Show.
The Mary Rose, flagship of Henry VIII of England that sank in 1545, is raised from the Solent.
Michael Jackson performs the Moonwalk for the first time while performing "Billie Jean" on the Motown 25 television special.
Emanuela Orlandi, a 15-year-old Vatican girl, mysteriously disappears in Rome while returning home from a music lesson.

South Africa announces "all outstanding issues" preventing independence for South West Africa (present-day Namibia) have been resolved, except for the continuing presence of 23,000 Cuban troops in neighboring Angola.
Gulf Air Flight 771 crashes in the United Arab Emirates after a bomb explodes in the baggage compartment, killing 117.
A North Korean Ilyushin Il-62M jet, en route to Conakry Airport in Guinea, crashes into the Fouta Djall Mountains of Guinea, killing all 23 people on board.
Pioneer 10 passes the orbit of Neptune, becoming the first human-made object to leave the vicinity of the major planets of the Solar System.
The migration of the ARPANET to TCP/IP is officially completed (this is considered to be the beginning of the true Internet).
Invasion of Grenada by United States troops at the behest of Eugenia Charles of Dominica, a member of the Organization of American States.
Leopold Kohr, the people of Belau, Amory and Hunter Lovins/Rocky Mountain Institute and Manfred Max Neef/CEPAUR win the Right Livelihood Award.
Maurice Bishop, Prime Minister of Grenada, and 40 others are assassinated in a military coup.
The Herreys' song "Diggi-Loo Diggi-Ley" wins the Eurovision Song Contest for Sweden in Luxembourg.
Liechtenstein becomes the last country in Europe to grant women the right to vote.
The African republic Upper Volta changes its name to Burkina Faso.
The Bornean Sultanate of Brunei gains full independence from the United Kingdom, having become a British protectorate in 1888.
The Sandinista Front wins the Nicaraguan general elections.
More than one million people, led by Tancredo Neves, occupy the streets of São Paulo to demand direct presidential elections during the Brazilian military government of João Figueiredo.
Tim Macartney-Snape and Greg Mortimer become the first Australians to reach the summit of Mount Everest.
Half a million people in Manila demonstrate against the regime of Ferdinand Marcos.
Hayim Association is founded by Rina Zaizov Marx and parents of children with cancer as paediatric oncology department in Israel.
Western Sahara conflict: Morocco leaves the Organization of African Unity in protest at the admission of Western Sahara as a member.
The 30th Eurovision Song Contest takes place in Gothenburg, Sweden and is won by the Bobbysocks! song La det swinge for Norway.
Heysel Stadium disaster: Thirty-nine spectators are killed in rioting on the terraces during the European Cup final between Liverpool F.C. and Juventus (0–1) at Heysel Stadium in Brussels, Belgium.
The Soviet Union performs a nuclear weapon test in eastern Kazakhstan.
TWA Flight 847, carrying 153 passengers from Athens to Rome, is hijacked by a Hezbollah fringe group.
Studio Ghibli, an animation studio, is founded in Tokyo.
American naturalist Dian Fossey is found brutally murdered in Rwanda.
Palace of Justice siege: Members of the 19th of April Movement (M-19) Marxist guerrilla group take over the Palace of Justice of Colombia in Bogotá and hold the Supreme Court hostage.
Gérard Hoarau, exiled political leader from the Seychelles, is assassinated in London.
Forty-four tornadoes hit Ohio, Pennsylvania, New York and Ontario, including a rare and powerful F5. In total, the event kills 90 people.
Greenland withdraws from the European Economic Community as a result of a new agreement on fishing rights.
Chernobyl disaster: A mishandled safety test at the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant in Pripyat, Ukrainian SSR, Soviet Union "killed at least 4,056 people and damaged almost $7 billion of property".
Construction of the Oosterscheldekering, the world's largest openable storm surge flood barrier, is completed in the Netherlands.
The Lake Nyos disaster, a limnic eruption, occurs in Cameroon, killing nearly 2,000 people.
The government of Ivory Coast requests international diplomatic use of the French form of its name, Côte d'Ivoire.
The Voyager 2 space probe makes its first encounter with Uranus.
Swedish Prime Minister Olof Palme is shot to death on his way home from the cinema in Stockholm, Sweden.
The Maxi Trial (Italian: Maxiprocesso) begins in the bunker room of the Ucciardone prison (Palermo).
In Istanbul, two Abu Nidal terrorists kill 22 and wound 6 inside the Neve Shalom Synagogue during Shabbat services.
The Marshall Islands became an associated state under the Compact of Free Association.
The cargo ship Khian Sea departs from the docks of Philadelphia, carrying 14,000 tons of toxic waste.
At the Prater Stadium of Vienna, Porto of Portugal defeats Bayern München of West Germany 2–1 and wins its first European Cup.
Michael Jackson releases Bad, his first studio album since Thriller, the best-selling album of all time.
In Burkina Faso, a military coup is orchestrated by Blaise Compaoré against incumbent President Thomas Sankara.
The United States establishes diplomatic relations with Mongolia.
A 6.9 magnitude earthquake occurs in Napo Province in northeast Ecuador, killing roughly 1,000 people.
A Soviet-made Ilyushin Il-62 airliner, operated by LOT Polish Airlines, crashes into a forest just outside Warsaw, killing all 183 people on board.
South African Airways Flight 295 crashes into the Indian Ocean off Mauritius, due to a fire in the cargo hold; the 159 passengers and crew perish.
Lieutenant Colonel Sitiveni Rabuka executes a bloodless coup in Fiji.
Two commuter trains collide head-on on the outskirts of Jakarta, Indonesia; 102 are killed.
Great Basin National Park is dedicated; it is the 49th national park in the United States and the first in the state of Nevada.
Benazir Bhutto is sworn in as Prime Minister of Pakistan, becoming the first woman to head the government of an Islam-dominated state.
Eritrean War of Independence – Battle of Afabet: The Nadew Command, an Ethiopian army corps in Eritrea, is attacked on 3 sides by military units of the Eritrean People's Liberation Front (EPLF).
Kuwait Airways Flight 422 is hijacked while en route from Bangkok, Thailand, to Kuwait.
Hurricane Gilbert devastates Jamaica; it turns towards Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula 2 days later, causing an estimated $5 billion in damage.
The Fatih Sultan Mehmet Bridge in Istanbul, Turkey, is completed, providing the second connection between the continents of Europe and Asia over the Bosphorus.
The Morris worm, the first computer worm distributed via the Internet, written by Robert Tappan Morris, is launched from Massachusetts Institute of Technology in the U.S.
The first McDonald's restaurant in a country run by a Communist party opens in Belgrade, Yugoslavia.
Israeli–Palestinian conflict: An independent State of Palestine is proclaimed at the Palestinian National Council meeting in Algiers, by a vote of 253–46.
The Piper Alpha production platform in the North Sea is destroyed by explosions and fires, killing 165 oil workers and 2 rescue mariners. 61 workers survive.
Roman Catholic Archbishop Marcel Lefebvre consecrates four bishops at Écône, Switzerland, for his apostolate, along with Bishop Antonio de Castro Mayer, without a papal mandate.
Eurosport, a multiple-language sports broadcasting station in Europe, begins broadcasting, from Issy-les-Moulineaux, Île-de-France, France.
Tbilisi massacre: Georgian demonstrators are massacred by Soviet Army soldiers in Tbilisi's central square during a peaceful rally; 20 citizens are killed, many injured.
Hans-Adam II becomes Prince of Liechtenstein on the death of his father, Prince Franz Joseph II.
The state funeral of Emperor Shōwa (Hirohito) in Tokyo is attended by leaders and representatives of 160 nations.
Elections are held in Namibia, leading to a victory for the South West Africa People's Organisation.
Alleged coup attempt in Burkina Faso by military officials foiled.
Representatives of the government of Ethiopia and Eritrean separatists meet in Atlanta, with former U.S. President Jimmy Carter attempting to broker a peace settlement.
Former Ugandan dictator Idi Amin is expelled to Senegal from Zaire after using a fake Zairean passport in an attempt to return to Uganda.
Students from Beijing, Shanghai, Xi'an and Nanjing begin protesting in Tiananmen Square in Beijing.
UTA Flight 772 explodes over Niger, killing all 171 people on board (the Islamic Jihad Organization claims responsibility).
Comet Austin makes its closest approach to the sun.
President of the United States George H. W. Bush gives his first State of the Union address and proposes that the U.S. and the Soviet Union make deep cuts to their military forces in Europe.
The 14th and final Extraordinary Congress of the Yugoslav Communist Party concludes after 3 days.
After 75 years of South African rule since World War I, Namibia becomes independent.
Pope John Paul II begins an eight-day tour of Cape Verde, Guinea-Bissau, Mali, Burkina Faso and Chad.
In Myanmar, the State Law and Order Restoration Council orders the arrest of Aung San Suu Kyi and five other political dissidents.
President Kenneth Kaunda agrees to allow multiparty elections in Zambia after 17 years of single-party rule.
Cold War: The leaders of the Yemen Arab Republic and the People's Democratic Republic of Yemen announce the unification of their countries as the Republic of Yemen.
The rebel Rwandan Patriotic Front invades Rwanda from Uganda, marking the start of the Rwandan Civil War.
The Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Nigeria, and Sierra Leone send peacekeepers to intervene in the First Liberian Civil War.
An Azerbaijani Mil Mi-8 helicopter carrying a 19-member peacekeeping mission team is shot down by Armenian military forces in Khojavend District, Azerbaijan.
Dissolution of the Soviet Union: Ukraine declares independence, followed by Belarus the next day, from the Soviet Union.
