In Paris, the Vietnam-backed government of the state of Cambodia signs an agreement with the Khmer Rouge to end the civil war and bring the Khmer Rouge into power despite its role in the Cambodian genocide.
Dissolution of the Soviet Union: Armenia declares independence from the Soviet Union.
Michael Jackson releases Dangerous, selling 5 million copies in the first week.
Dissolution of Yugoslavia: Croatia and Slovenia declare their independence from Yugoslavia.
Dissolution of Yugoslavia: The Republic of Macedonia becomes independent, beginning a name dispute with Greece.
In West Germany, the Bundestag votes to move the capital from Bonn to Berlin.
Argentina, Brazil, Uruguay and Paraguay sign the Treaty of Asunción, establishing Mercosur.
Dissolution of the Soviet Union: Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan declare their independence; Tajikistan follows suit on September 9.
Ukraine and four other nations in the Commonwealth of Independent States reject Russia's proposal to maintain unified armed forces.
Abkhazia declares independence from Georgia.
The Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia begins to break up; Slovenia and Croatia gain independence and international recognition in some Western countries.
Ownership of the port town of Walvis Bay is transferred from South Africa to Namibia.
In Paraguay the National Constituent Assembly approves the new Constitution of Paraguay.
In Mauritania, security forces open fire on violent extremist opponents of President of Mauritania Maaouya Ould Sid'Ahmed Taya, allegedly killing at least four people.
The government of Mozambique signs the Rome General Peace Accords with leaders of RENAMO, ending the 16-year-old Mozambican Civil War.
In Miami, former Panamanian dictator Manuel Noriega is sentenced to 40 years in prison for participating in the illegal drug trade and racketeering.
Mauritius becomes a republic while remaining a member of the Commonwealth of Nations.
El Salvador officials and rebel leaders sign the Chapultepec Peace Accords in Mexico City, ending the 12-year Salvadoran Civil War that claimed at least 75,000 lives.
A wildfire on the Greek island of Ikaria kills 13.

Abortion in Poland: Lech Walesa signs into law one of the strictest anti-abortion laws in Eastern Europe, banning abortion for any reason other than rape, incest, genetic deformity, or if the mother's life is in danger.
The Majilis of Kazakhstan approves the nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty and agrees to dismantle the more than 100 missiles left on its territory by the fall of the USSR.
An Avioimpex Yakovlev Yak-42D crashes into Mount Trojani near Ohrid, North Macedonia.
Eritrea and Monaco gain entry to the United Nations.
Eritrea gains independence from Ethiopia.
Mongolia holds its first direct presidential elections, Punsalmaagiin Ochirbat remains president.
A coup in Burundi results in the death of president Melchior Ndadaye and sparks the Burundi Civil War.
Mahamane Ousmane is elected president of Niger.

Iraq disarmament crisis: Iraq refuses to allow UNSCOM inspectors to use its own aircraft to fly into Iraq and begins military operations in the demilitarized zone between Iraq and Kuwait, and the northern Iraqi no-fly zones.
The Bishkek Protocol between Armenia and Azerbaijan is signed in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, effectively freezing the Nagorno-Karabakh conflict.
In Slovakia, populist leader Vladimír Mečiar wins the general election.
A referendum in Moldova results in the electorate voting against possible reunification with Romania.
Rwandan President Juvénal Habyarimana and Burundi President Cyprien Ntaryamira die when a missile shoots down their jet near Kigali, Rwanda.
The Red Cross estimates that hundreds of thousands of Tutsi have been killed in Rwanda.
October – Iraq disarmament crisis: Iraq threatens to stop cooperating with UNSCOM inspectors and begins to once again deploy troops near its border with Kuwait.
Malawi holds its first multiparty elections.
Hurricane Gordon hits Central America, Jamaica, Cuba, the Bahamas, Haiti and the Southeastern United States, causing $594 million in damages and 1,152 fatalities.
Nelson Mandela is inaugurated as South Africa's first black president.
AMIA bombing: In Buenos Aires, a terrorist attack destroys a building housing several Jewish organizations, killing 85 and injuring many more.
Quebec independentists narrowly lose a referendum for a mandate to negotiate independence from Canada.
A fire in Baku Metro, Azerbaijan, kills 289 passengers, becoming the world's worst subway disaster.
Astronaut Norman Thagard becomes the first American to ride into space aboard a Russian launch vehicle (the Soyuz TM-21), lifting off from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan.
Eduard Shevardnadze, the Georgian head of state, survives an assassination attempt in Tbilisi.
Michael Jackson releases his double album HIStory: Past, Present and Future, Book I.
NASA's Galileo probe enters Jupiter's atmosphere.
The United States government stops funding the NSFNET, making the Internet a wholly privatized system.
Iraq disarmament crisis: Iraqi scuba divers, under the direction of the United Nations Special Commission, dredge the Tigris near Baghdad.
TAROM Flight 371 from Bucharest to Brussels crashes shortly after takeoff, killing all 60 people on board.
The Indian government officially renames the city of Bombay, restoring the name Mumbai.
The American Embassy in Athens, Greece, comes under mortar fire.
The government of New Zealand agrees to pay $130 million worth of compensation for the loss of land suffered by the Māori population between the years of 1844 and 1864.
Data sent back by the Galileo space probe indicates there may be water on one of Jupiter's moons.
Iraq disarmament crisis: UNSCOM inspectors uncover buried prohibited missile parts.
The MV Bukoba sinks in Tanzanian waters in Lake Victoria, killing nearly 1,000 people in one of Africa's worst maritime disasters.
Robert Mugabe is re-elected as President of Zimbabwe, although only 32% of the electorate actually voted.
Frederick Chiluba is re-elected as President of Zambia.
Burundian Civil War: massacres of Hutus by Tutsis in Burundi take place with more than 450 killed within a few days.
Colonel Ibrahim Baré Maïnassara deposes the first democratically elected President of Niger, Mahamane Ousmane, in a military coup.
First Liberian Civil War: fighting breaks out in Monrovia, Liberia, between various rebel factions struggling for power in the country's interrupted civil war.
The Norwegian parliamentary election is held in Norway.
The capital of Kazakhstan is moved from Almaty to Astana.
In northwest Rwanda, Hutu militia members kill 6 Spanish aid workers and three soldiers, and seriously wound another.
A military coup in Sierra Leone replaces President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah with Major Johnny Paul Koroma.
The United Kingdom hands sovereignty of the British colony in Hong Kong to the People's Republic of China.
Janet Jagan (widow of Cheddi Jagan) takes office in Guyana.
Sandline affair: Australian newspapers publish stories that the government of Papua New Guinea has brought mercenaries onto Bougainville Island.
Scotland votes in favour of a devolved Parliament, forming the Scottish Parliament less than two years later.
Wales votes in favour of devolution and the formation of a National Assembly for Wales.
In Ottawa (Canada) representatives from 121 countries sign a treaty prohibiting the manufacture and deployment of anti-personnel land mines.
A Russian Proton rocket is launched from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan, carrying the first segment of the International Space Station, the 21-ton Zarya Module.

Rome Statute: at a conference in Rome, 120 countries vote to create a permanent International Criminal Court to prosecute individuals for genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes, and the crime of aggression.

Benoit Lecomte finishes his 72-day swim across the Atlantic Ocean, but uncertainty over the exact route and distance covered prevent him from being recognized as the first person to swim across the Atlantic.
The World Bank praises Costa Rica for its remarkable success in raising life expectancy and lowering infant mortality.

Iraq disarmament crisis: Iraqi President Saddam Hussein negotiates a deal with U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan, allowing weapons inspectors to return to Baghdad, preventing military action by the United States and United Kingdom.
Eschede train disaster: an Intercity-Express high-speed train derails between Hanover and Hamburg, Germany, causing 101 deaths.
Google, Inc. is founded in Menlo Park, California, by Stanford University PhD candidates Larry Page and Sergey Brin.
The Cuban Five intelligence agents are arrested in Miami, and later convicted of espionage.
The Department of Justice files an antitrust lawsuit against Microsoft, alleging its Windows operating system unfairly takes market share from Netscape's Navigator.
Hugo Chávez, politician and former officer of the Venezuelan army, is elected President of Venezuela.
Former Warsaw Pact members Hungary, Poland, and the Czech Republic join NATO.
Armenian parliament shooting: Gunmen open fire in Armenia's National Assembly building, killing Prime Minister Vazgen Sargsyan, Parliament Chairman Karen Demirchyan, and six other members.
One of four bombs detonated in Lusaka, Zambia, which destroys the Angolan Embassy.
The King of Bhutan allows television transmissions to commence in the Kingdom for the first time, coinciding with the King's Silver Jubilee.
In Uzbekistan, an apparent assassination attempt against President Islam Karimov takes place at government headquarters.
Ibrahim Baré Maïnassara, president of Niger, is assassinated.
Rwandan Hutu rebels kill and dismember eight foreign tourists at the Buhoma homestead, Uganda.
In Guinea-Bissau, President João Bernardo Vieira is ousted in a military coup.
With the Torrijos–Carter Treaties being put into effect on this day, Panama gains full control of the Canal.
After 22 years of restoration work, Leonardo da Vinci's The Last Supper is placed back on display in Milan, Italy.
The Øresund Bridge between Denmark and Sweden is officially opened for traffic.

Air France Flight 4590, a scheduled Concorde supersonic jet flight that crashed shortly after takeoff from Paris, France following a fire on the back of the aircraft, killing all 109 people aboard and four on the ground.
Kenya Airways Flight 431 crashes off the Ivory Coast into the Atlantic Ocean, killing 169 people.
The United States dollar becomes the official currency of Ecuador, replacing the Ecuadorian sucre.
Torrential rains in Africa led to the worst flooding in Mozambique in 50 years, which lasts until March and kills 800 people.
A rare conjunction of seven celestial bodies (Sun, Moon, planets Mercury–Saturn) occurs during the new moon.
The state funeral of Abulfaz Elchibey, the second President of Azerbaijan, takes place in Baku.
The Second Intifada civilian uprising in Jerusalem and Palestine proper.
Steve Jobs introduces the Mac OS X Public Beta for US$29.95.
UNESCO holds the inaugural celebration of International Mother Language Day.
Wikipedia, which became the world's largest encyclopedia, is launched.
Armenia and Azerbaijan join the Council of Europe.
A self-immolation incident takes place in Tiananmen Square in central Beijing, China.

George W. Bush, president of the United States, delivers remarks at the Islamic Center of Washington praising Muslim Americans and condemning Islamophobia in the aftermath of the September 11 attacks.
Sherpa Temba Tsheri, 15, becomes the youngest person to reach the summit of Mount Everest.
The Budapest Convention on Cybercrime, the first international treaty to address cybercrime, is signed in Budapest, Hungary.
Tropical Storm Allison hits the U.S. state of Texas, severely flooding Houston and killing 23 people.
Fall of Kabul: Northern Alliance forces take the Afghan capital Kabul.
The African Union is formed to replace the Organisation of African Unity.
Tropical Storm Vamei forms within 1.5 degrees of the equator.
General Robert Guéï leads an army mutiny in an attempt to overthrow Ivory Coast President Laurent Gbagbo, resulting in civil war.
American president George W. Bush defines an axis of evil consisting of Iran, Iraq, and North Korea in his State of the Union Address.
The Organisation of African Unity is disbanded and replaced by the African Union.
The Euro is introduced as the official physical currency in the Eurozone countries.
The Bibliotheca Alexandrina opens in Alexandria, Egypt, in a ceremony attended by several heads of state.
Rebels bombard Arthington, Liberia, with artillery during the Second Liberian Civil War causing panic in the neighboring capital, Monrovia.
Siege of the Church of the Nativity in Bethlehem: Israeli forces besiege the Church of the Nativity in Bethlehem when militants take shelter there.
President Hugo Chávez of Venezuela is restored to power following an attempted coup.
Erfurt school massacre: An expelled student kills 16 people and commits suicide at a school in Erfurt, Germany.
In response to increasingly common attacks by Palestinian militants, Israeli initiates Operation Defensive Shield, a large-scale counter-terrorism operation in the West Bank.
Slovakia approves joining the European Union in a referendum.
Slovenia approves joining the European Union and NATO in a referendum.
The World Health Organization issues a global alert on SARS when it spreads to Hong Kong and Vietnam after originating in Mainland China.
U.S. President George W. Bush presents a 48-hour ultimatum for Iraqi president Saddam Hussein to resign.
At the conclusion of the STS-107 mission, the Space Shuttle Columbia disintegrates during reentry over Texas, killing all seven astronauts on board.
A series of car bombings occur in Baghdad, Iraq, targeting multiple police stations and a Red Cross headquarters.
Car bombs explode at Gateway of India and Zaveri Bazaar in Mumbai, claiming 54 lives and injuring 244 others.
Hurricane Isabel makes landfall in North Carolina.
SMART-1, an ESA spaceprobe and ESA's first mission to the moon, is launched from Kourou, French Guiana.
SCO Group files a lawsuit against IBM as part of an ongoing dispute regarding the use of Unix in the development of Linux.
Bulgaria, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Romania, Slovakia and Slovenia are admitted to NATO, the largest expansion of the organization.
NASA's MESSENGER space probe is launched, with its primary mission being the study of Mercury.
The Cassini–Huygens orbiter reaches the orbit of Saturn.
Facebook, originally called TheFacebook, is launched by Mark Zuckerberg.
Armed robbers steal Edvard Munch's The Scream, Madonna, and other paintings from the Munch Museum in Oslo, Norway.
The Genesis space probe crash-lands in Utah after a three-year study of the Sun.
Google makes its initial public offering.
Suicide bombers detonate two bombs at the Red Sea resort of Taba, Egypt, killing 34 people and injuring 171, mostly Israeli tourists.
Bombings attributed to the Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan kill 15 in Tashkent, the capital of Uzbekistan.
The Seattle Central Library opens in Seattle, Washington.
In Kazakhstan, Zamanbek Nurkadilov, former mayor of Almaty, government minister and a political opponent of Nursultan Nazarbayev is found dead at his family compound.
Uzbek Interior Ministry and National Security Service troops massacre at least 200 protesters in the city of Andijan.
English whisky is re-established in England.
The Huygens spacecraft lands on Titan, the largest moon of Saturn.
Helios Airways Flight 522, en route from Larnaca, Cyprus to Prague, Czech Republic via Athens, crashes in the hills near Grammatiko, Greece, killing 121 passengers and crew.
The first ever YouTube video is uploaded, titled Me at the zoo.
The Al-Aimmah bridge disaster in Baghdad, Iraq kills 953 Shia Muslim pilgrims who were celebrating a religious festival.
Deep Impact is launched from Cape Canaveral with the purpose of studying the comet Tempel 1.
Angela Merkel assumes office as the first female Chancellor of Germany.
At least 60 people are killed and 115 more are wounded in a series of coordinated suicide bombings in Amman, Jordan.
Montenegro declares its independence.
The International Astronomical Union defines 'planet' at its 26th General Assembly, removing Pluto's status as a planet and reclassifying it as a dwarf planet 76 years after its discovery.
NASA's Cassini–Huygens spacecraft announces a geyser-like emission of vapor, dust, and small ice crystals on Saturn's moon Enceladus, possibly indicating the presence of water.
In Buenos Aires, Argentina, serial shooter Martín Ríos opens fire against passers-by on Cabildo Avenue, killing an 18-year-old and injuring six others.
A series of car bombs and mortar attacks in Sadr City, Baghdad, kills at least 215 people and injure 257 other people.
NASA launches the first interplanetary space probe to Pluto, the New Horizons.
A series of seven bomb blasts hits the city of Mumbai, India, killing more than 200 people.
NASA's Stardust mission successfully ends, the first to return dust from a comet.
Typhoon Xangsane passed Manila on its way to causing more than 300 deaths, mostly in the Philippines and Vietnam.
Microblogging and social networking service website Twitter(now known as X) was launched.
British three-year-old Madeleine McCann disappears in Praia da Luz, Lagos, Portugal, described by The Daily Telegraph as "the most heavily reported missing-person case in modern history".
Mount Ruapehu in Tongariro National Park in New Zealand, erupts.
Georgia accuses three Russian helicopters of firing on the Kodori Gorge, then the only part of the break-away autonomous republic of Abkhazia still under Georgian control.
The Czech Republic, Estonia, Hungary, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Poland, Slovakia, and Slovenia join the Schengen border-free zone.
Bulgaria and Romania join the European Union, while Slovenia joins the Eurozone.
Montenegro adopts a new constitution, which among other things changes the country's official name from "Republic of Montenegro" to "Montenegro".
Anti-government protests in Myanmar suppressed by ruling junta.
October 21 – The 17th National Congress of the Chinese Communist Party is held in Beijing, China.
Hurricane Noel killed 223 and carved a path of destruction across the Atlantic Ocean.
NASA's MESSENGER spacecraft makes its second fly-by of Venus on route to Mercury.
The Russo-Georgian War took place between Russia and Georgia.
The Union of South American Nations, an intergovernmental organization between states in South America, is founded.
Bhutan holds its first-ever general elections following the adoption of a new Constitution which changed the country from an absolute monarchy to a multiparty democracy.
Cyclone Nargis kills 138,000 people in Myanmar.
The Quito Ultratumba nightclub fire in Quito, Ecuador, kills 19 people and injures at least 24 more.
President Sidi Ould Cheikh Abdallahi of Mauritania is deposed in a military coup d'état.
A military coup d'état deposes the government of Guinea shortly after the death of longtime President Lansana Conté.
At 19:04:39 UTC, the uncrewed MESSENGER space probe is at its closest approach during its first flyby of the planet Mercury.
African Union and Comoros forces invade the rebel-held island of Anjouan, returning the island to Comorian control.
XL Airways Germany Flight 888T. An Airbus A320 due to be redelivered to Air New Zealand stalls and crashes over Mediterranean Sea resulting the deaths of 7.
The Czech Republic becomes the final member-state of the European Union to sign the Treaty of Lisbon, thereby permitting that document's initiation into European law.
Caspian Airlines Flight 7908, en route from Tehran, Iran, to Yerevan, Armenia crashes into the Jannatabad village in Qazvin Province; killing all 168 on board.
March 5 - Michael Jackson announces his This Is It concert residency in London, England.
Slovakia adopts the euro as its national currency, replacing the Slovak koruna.
The President of Madagascar, Marc Ravalomanana, is overthrown in a coup d'état, following a month of unrest in Antananarivo.
At least five people are killed and 275 injured in a train crash near Yaoundé, Cameroon. (BBC) (Press TV).
Asunción, the capital of Paraguay, becomes the American Capital of Culture and Vilnius and Linz become the European Capitals of Culture.
Barack Obama is sworn in as the 44th President of the United States, becoming the first African-American to hold the office.
The President of Guinea-Bissau, João Bernardo Vieira, is assassinated during an armed attack on his residence in Bissau.
Amateur astronomer Anthony Wesley is the first to report that a new dark spot has developed on the planet Jupiter.
Two trains collide in Halle, Belgium, killing 19 and injuring 171 people.

The European Union agree to an €85 billion rescue deal for Ireland from the European Financial Stability Facility, the International Monetary Fund and bilateral loans from the United Kingdom, Denmark and Sweden.
A 7.1 magnitude earthquake rocks Christchurch, New Zealand causing large amounts of damage but no direct fatalities.
Slovenia becomes the 32nd member of the OECD.
Kyrgyz President Kurmanbek Bakiyev flees the country amid fierce anti-government riots in the capital, Bishkek.
The tallest man-made structure to date, the Burj Khalifa in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, is officially opened.
Researchers at CERN trap 38 antihydrogen atoms for a sixth of a second, marking the first time in history that humans have trapped antimatter.
Protests in Bangkok, Thailand, end with a bloody military crackdown, killing 91 and injuring more than 2,100.
Nude, Green Leaves and Bust by Pablo Picasso sells in New York for US$106.5 million, setting another new world record for a work of art sold at auction.
An 8.8-magnitude earthquake occurs in Chile, triggering a tsunami over the Pacific and killing at least 525. The earthquake is one of the largest in recorded history.
The Nintendo 3DS has its first release in Japan, following later releases in Europe on March 25, North America on March 27, and Australia on March 31.

In Norway, Anders Behring Breivik kills 8 people in a bomb blast which targeted government buildings in central Oslo, then kills 69 at a massacre at a Workers' Youth League camp on the island of Utøya.
Juno, the first solar-powered spacecraft on a mission to Jupiter, is launched from Cape Canaveral Air Force Station.
Celebrating the independence of South Sudan, the world's newest country.
The planet Neptune completes its first orbit since it was discovered in 1846.
Samoa and Tokelau move from east to west of the International Date Line, thereby skipping December 30, in order to align their time zones better with their main trading partners.
Approximately 100 people die after a petrol pipeline explodes in Nairobi.
Anti-government protests known as the "Arab Spring" spread across the Middle East and North Africa, sparking revolutions in Tunisia, Egypt, Libya, Yemen, and Syria.
Manx2 Flight 7100, a Fairchild Metro III, crashes on its third attempt at landing at Cork airport, Ireland from Belfast.
U.S. national security team gathered in the White House Situation Room to monitor progress of Operation Neptune Spear, resulting in the death of Al-Qaeda leader Osama bin Laden.

As part of a series of protests against the Stop Online Piracy Act and the PROTECT IP Act, the English Wikipedia, along with other websites, goes dark for 24 hours, starting at midnight Eastern Standard Time (05:00 UTC).

Legislative elections are held in Greece to elect all 300 members of the Hellenic Parliament and the New Democracy party led by Antonis Samaras, comes out as the largest party winning 108 out of 300 seats.
The National Movement for the Liberation of Azawad unilaterally declares the independence of Azawad from Mali.
Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh formally transfers power to Vice President Abdrabbuh Mansur Hadi, after a year of mass protests, ending his 33-year-long reign.
A series of explosions is reported at a munitions dump in Brazzaville, the capital of the Republic of the Congo, with at least 250 people dead.
Mutinous soldiers in Guinea-Bissau stage a coup d'état and take control of the capital city, Bissau.

The Voyager 1 space probe becomes the first human-made object to successfully exit the Solar System and enter Interstellar space, and to an extent, becoming the first Interstellar probe, pioneering Interstellar exploration.

Canada officially cuts diplomatic ties with Iran by closing its embassy in Tehran, and orders the expulsion of Iranian diplomats from Ottawa, over support for Syria, nuclear plans and human rights abuses.
The U.S. state of Washington becomes the first jurisdiction in the modern world to officially legalize the possession of cannabis for personal use.
The UN General Assembly approves a motion granting Palestine non-member observer state status.
Severe weather spawns eight tornadoes across southern Mississippi and southwest Alabama, including an EF4 tornado which struck the city of Hattiesburg, Mississippi.
Smoke rises as a result of the Westgate shopping mall attack in Nairobi, Kenya, carried out by Al-Shabaab militants.
American scientists use a 3D printer to create a living lab-grown ear from collagen and animal ear cell cultures.
A tornado outbreak occurs in Illinois, United States.
A magnitude 7.2 earthquake struck Bohol, Philippines, leaving 222 dead, 8 missing, and 976 people injured.
An EF5 tornado in the US state of Oklahoma hits Moore and several other surrounding areas near Oklahoma City, resulting in 24 deaths and many injuries.
The Emergency Alert Systems of five different television stations across the U.S. states of Montana, Michigan, Wisconsin, and New Mexico are hijacked, airing a false "Zombie apocalypse" hoax.

Cardinal Jorge Mario Bergoglio of Argentina is elected the 266th pope, whereupon he takes the name Francis and becomes the first Jesuit pope, the first pope from the Americas, and the first pope from the Southern Hemisphere.
Benedict XVI resigns as pope, becoming the first to do so since Gregory XII in 1415, and the first to do so voluntarily since Celestine V in 1294.

Delegates from some 140 countries and territories sign the Minamata Treaty, a UNEP treaty designed to protect human health and the environment from emissions and releases of mercury and mercury compounds.
Longtime Burkina Faso President Blaise Compaoré resigns after widespread protests in response to his attempts to abolish presidential term limits.
Air Algérie Flight 5017, a McDonnell Douglas MD-83, crashes in Mali, killing all 116 people on board.
U.S. President Barack Obama announces the resumption of normal diplomatic relations between the U.S. and Cuba.
Nicolás Maduro, the President of Venezuela, severs diplomatic and political ties with Panama, accusing Panama of being involved in a conspiracy against the Venezuelan government.
Malaysia Airlines Flight 370, a Boeing 777 airliner en route to Beijing from Kuala Lumpur, disappears over the Gulf of Thailand with 239 people on board.

Revolution of Dignity: The Verkhovna Rada (Ukrainian parliament) votes to remove President Viktor Yanukovych from office, replacing him with Oleksandr Turchynov, after days of civil unrest leaving around 100 people dead in Kyiv.
Two hostages and terrorist Man Haron Monis are killed in the Lindt Cafe siege in Sydney, Australia.
Mount Ontake, in Japan, erupts, killing several climbers on the slopes of the volcano.

According to a South Korea Unification Ministry report, a twenty-three story apartment building collapsed in Pyongchon-guyok, Pyongyang, North Korea (DPR of Korea), with more than 490 fatalities estimated.
Crimea is annexed by Russia, starting the Russo-Ukrainian war.
Greek government-debt crisis: Greece becomes the first advanced economy to miss a payment to the International Monetary Fund in the 71-year history of the IMF.
A UAE military intelligence operation in the country of Yemen frees one British hostage.
After Houthi forces seize the presidential palace, Yemeni President Abd Rabbuh Mansur Hadi resigns after months of unrest.
The World Health Organization (WHO) declares that rubella has been eradicated from the Americas.
Metrojet Flight 9268, an Airbus A321 airliner en route to Saint Petersburg from Sharm el-Sheikh, crashes near Al-Hasana in Sinai, killing all 217 passengers and 7 crew members on board.
In Tonga, the Mata ʻo e Laʻa Solar Facility is officially opened by King Tupou VI.
NASA's New Horizons spacecraft performs a close flyby of Pluto, becoming the first spacecraft in history to visit the distant world.
A crush during the Hajj pilgrimage in Mecca kills at least 2,200 people and injures more than 900 others, with more than 650 missing.
OpenAI, a non-profit artificial intelligence research company, is founded.
CCP general secretary Xi Jinping and ROC president Ma Ying-jeou formally meet for the first time.
